findings.requirement: AC5: Композиция «в дополнение, не вместо» (composition backstop)
findings.detail: Whether the 7-day set-overlap backstop ALSO runs after the new pair-rule produces a BROAD soft-flag (not just after a no-match/no-series/toggle-off pass) is genuinely ambiguous, and two independent readings of this same tech-spec disagree. Decision 3 states the rule as 'if it does NOT hard-block, ALWAYS run the existing 7-day set-overlap dedup' — a broad flag is not a hard-block, so by this literal wording the backstop should ALSO run after a broad flag (possibly firing a second, contradictory E015/E014 for the same article). Architecture 'How it works' step 3 restates the same gate as 'If the pair-rule neither blocked NOR is disabled/empty → fall through to backstop' — read as a strict AND-condition this would SKIP the backstop specifically in the broad-flag case (pairs non-empty, rule enabled, not blocked), which is the opposite behaviour. This is not a theoretical nitpick: the independently-run test-reviewer pass on this same tech-spec (work/dedup-model-series/logs/techspec/test-reviewer-review.json) recommends a scenario asserting 'broad-pair soft-flag -> exactly one E014, article published, and the set-overlap backstop is NOT additionally invoked (no second ping, no block)' — i.e. a reviewer reading the same document independently concluded the OPPOSITE of Decision 3's literal text. The user-spec's own AC5 wording ('нет совпадения / нет серии / выключено') is itself ambiguous on whether 'нет совпадения' means 'no match of any kind' or 'no DISTINCTIVE match' (broad counts as a match). The Testing Strategy's only broad-flag test ('flag [E014], article publishes (NOT blocked)') is compatible with either interpretation as long as the fixture's old-rule overlap happens to stay under 0.50 — it does not pin down whether the backstop ran-but-passed or was skipped entirely. Left unresolved, an implementer could ship either interpretation and both existing reviewers would accept it, one of which regresses AC5's 'без изменений' guarantee for the common broad-recurring-line case (old dedup silently stops catching what it used to catch) or produces a confusing double-ping (E014 'will publish' immediately followed by E015 'blocked').
findings.recommendation: Add one explicit sentence to Decision 3 (and align Architecture step 3's wording with it) stating unambiguously whether a broad/soft-flag verdict from the pair-rule suppresses the old 7-day backstop or not, then add a dedicated integration test for exactly that combination (broad-pair match seeded together with an old-rule-qualifying ≥0.50 set-overlap candidate) so the composition behaviour is pinned rather than incidental to fixture choice.

findings.detail: Architecture's 'What we're building/modifying' section states admin_alerts.py's '[E014]/[E016] reused unchanged' — i.e. the broad-tier flag is meant to call the existing alert_cross_source_dupe(new_link, existing_link, new_source, existing_source, overlap_pct, n_matches, n_total, models) builder verbatim. That builder's fields (overlap_pct, n_matches/n_total, models list) are all car-model-overlap-specific, computed by the OLD set-overlap Jaccard comparison. The new pair-rule's flagship broad case is a theme-only match with NO shared model at all (e.g. '*|stranger things|B', exactly user-spec Scenario 3, called out there as 'главное замечание валидатора'). The tech-spec never specifies what values a theme-only broad match would supply for these four model-overlap-shaped parameters, so the operator ping for the very case the feature exists to catch risks rendering as an empty/misleading 'Совпадение моделей: 0% (0/0), Общие модели: (none)' with no mention of the actual matched series/theme — or, if computed naively (e.g. percentage from n_total=0), risks a runtime exception that the surrounding try/except would silently reroute into degraded-mode ([E016]) reporting instead of the intended broad-flag ([E014]) reporting, masking that the mechanism is actually working as designed.
findings.recommendation: Either extend alert_cross_source_dupe (or add a parallel builder) to accept and render the matched series/theme name for pair-rule-originated flags, or explicitly define in a Decision how the existing model-overlap fields are populated for a theme-only broad match (e.g. models=[shared model] if present else [], and what overlap_pct/n_total mean for a pure theme match). Add this exact scenario (broad THEME-ONLY match, no shared model) to the Testing Strategy — currently only 'Broad/theme-only match -> flag [E014]' is named without asserting on ping content.

findings.detail: Decision 7's rationale line ends 'Serves AC9, AC10.' AC9 in user-spec is the degraded-mode requirement (any mechanism failure -> ERROR + rate-limited [E016] + publish), which is unrelated to backfill/cold-DB handling; Decision 7 is entirely about the backfill re-select widening and pre-deploy cold-DB check, i.e. AC10 only. This is a citation slip, not a functional gap (AC9/degraded-mode is separately and correctly covered elsewhere), but it is exactly the kind of traceability mismatch that misleads a future reader auditing which Decision covers which AC.
findings.recommendation: Fix the citation in Decision 7 to 'Serves AC10' (drop AC9).

findings.requirement: AC7: Фейл-сейф — неизвестная/новая/неоднозначная серия -> широкий тир
findings.detail: Given the Ограничения constraint of regex + lexicons only (no LLM, no fuzzy NLP), the ONLY thing the extractor can structurally recognise as 'a series' is a lexicon match; a truly novel franchise name that isn't in SERIES_LEXICON at all can't be extracted as a series in the first place, so it can never reach the tier classifier to be defaulted to broad — it just produces no 'series' entry (same as no-theme). Decision 2's '_SERIES_DEFAULT_TIER="broad"' fail-safe therefore only protects lexicon entries that exist but weren't explicitly tagged distinctive/broad, not user-spec's literal phrasing of 'неизвестная, новая ... серия'. This is very likely the only implementable reading of AC7 given the stack constraints, and is probably what was intended, but the tech-spec never states this interpretation explicitly, which could confuse a future reader comparing AC7's user-spec wording against the implementation.
findings.recommendation: Add one clarifying sentence to Decision 2 stating explicitly that the fail-safe default covers 'lexicon entries without an explicit tier tag,' not text the lexicon fails to recognise as a series at all (which is out of scope by construction, per the no-LLM constraint).

summary: 9/11 ACs covered, 2 partial (AC4, AC5), 0 missing. The three risk areas the orchestrator flagged by name (fail-safe polarity, the two same-source/any-source behaviour reversals, cold-prod-DB backfill) are all thoroughly and correctly addressed — each has a dedicated Decision, an explicit Risks-table mitigation, and a named test. No scope creep, no YAGNI abstractions, no unjustified/undocumented deviations (both [TECHNICAL] decisions are genuinely non-deviating and their 'None' Deviations entry is defensible); Solution/Architecture sections have real technical depth (not a paraphrase). One CRITICAL finding: the composition backstop's behaviour after a BROAD/soft-flag verdict (does the old 7-day set-overlap dedup also run, or is it suppressed?) is ambiguously specified — Decision 3's literal text and Architecture step 3's literal text point opposite ways, and an independently-run test-reviewer pass on this same document assumed the opposite reading from Decision 3, confirming this is a real, not hypothetical, ambiguity in a core AC5 requirement. One MAJOR finding: the broad-tier [E014] ping is planned to reuse the old model-overlap-shaped builder unchanged, but the flagship broad case (theme-only, no shared model) doesn't naturally fit that builder's parameters, risking an uninformative or crashing ping for exactly the scenario the user-spec calls its main point. Two MINOR documentation nits (a mis-cited AC in Decision 7; an unstated interpretation of 'unknown series' in AC7's fail-safe).
